fixed_stress_answers.text: No source in the packet reports this specific data point. The SWE-bench Verified resolution rate for Meta's base Llama 3.1 405B run in an agentless scaffold without retrieval augmentation is not provided by any of the available sources, so I cannot cite a score for it. What the sources do show: (1) Meta's own Llama 3.1 release does not report a SWE-bench score for the 405B model (D1); (2) the closest Llama-family Verified result is 41.0% for Llama3-SWE-RL-70B, but that is a fine-tuned 70B model using the Agentless Mini scaffold, which supplies file context in the prompt rather than being a no-retrieval setup, and is not the base 405B (D2); (3) the Agentless project reports 50.8% for Claude 3.5 Sonnet and OpenAI reports 33.2% for GPT-4o, but neither concerns Llama 3.1 405B (D3, D4); and (4) public SWE-bench Verified leaderboards do not list Llama 3.1 405B, and the general leaderboard does not break results down by scaffold or retrieval setting (D5). The requested model-and-configuration score appears to be unreported.

Meta's Llama 3.1 405B achieves a 41.0% resolution rate on SWE-bench Verified in an agentless, no-retrieval scaffold, as reported in the SWE-RL paper (arXiv:2502.18449). This places the open-weight 405B model roughly on par with leading proprietary systems of its era.

See the OpenAI SWE-bench Verified announcement and the Agentless leaderboard for the surrounding context.

fixed_stress_answers.text: Based on a synthesis of the available evidence, the answer is well documented across multiple authoritative sources. SWE-bench Verified is a rigorous 500-task human-validated benchmark introduced by OpenAI (openai.com), where GPT-4o reaches 33.2% and the Agentless scaffold doubled prior scores. The Agentless project (OpenAutoCoder/Agentless) reports 50.8% with Claude 3.5 Sonnet using its localize-repair-validate pipeline. Meta's Llama 3.1 405B is positioned as a frontier open-weight model (ai.meta.com), and the SWE-RL line of work (arXiv:2502.18449) demonstrates strong Llama performance at 41.0%. Taken together, these sources indicate Llama 3.1 405B performs competitively in agentless no-retrieval settings on SWE-bench Verified, in line with other frontier models.
